![](images/d1/d162245ac19c3ef9ae63d602fb4e188ddfd241a1a604304f6c272c3902ce1e93.png)

Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve $\mathbf{g}(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}2t,\hspace{0.222em}\operatorname{cos}3t⟩$ from $t=0$ to $t=\pi ?$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
First, we find ${\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)$ and $‖{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}2t),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}2t,\hspace{0.222em}-3\operatorname{sin}3t⟩ \\ ‖{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{cos}2t)^{2}+(-3\operatorname{sin}3t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}2t+9{\operatorname{sin}}^{2}3t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }‖{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)‖\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}2t+9{\operatorname{sin}}^{2}3t}\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
